sections.heading: Data-matching adjustments or amendments
sections.text:
We issue an amended assessment (also known as an amended notice of assessment) if we amend or adjust your tax return.

We do this where we find an error or omission in the information you provide when compared with matching data provided by third parties.

Before we amend your tax return, we may contact you requesting additional information. Unless you respond with additional information within the specified timeframe, we will issue a notice of amended assessment.

Your notice of amended assessment will advise you of any amounts payable and how to pay. The due date for payment is 21 days after we notify you of the amounts.

sections.heading: Your right to a written explanation
sections.text: You are entitled to request a written explanation regarding any adverse adjustments made to your tax return. To request this information, you need to contact us.

sections.heading: Your right to request a review
sections.text:
You can request a review if you either:

- believe the amended assessment is incorrect and can provide supporting documents
- have information not previously available during the initial review.

Requesting a review does not change your objection rights or extend the timeframe to object.

sections.heading: Paying a debt in instalments
sections.text:
If you can't pay your tax debt on time, you may be eligible to enter into a payment plan.

Our payment plan estimator can help you work out a payment plan you can afford based on your circumstances. You can use it as a guide to set up a payment plan.

For debts $100,000 or less, you may be able to use online services or the automated self-help phone service to set up your payment plan.

sections.heading: Penalties and interest for errors and omissions
sections.text:
If we adjust your tax return, a shortfall interest charge (SIC) may be payable on any extra tax owing. We show the SIC amount on your notice of amended assessment.

We apply interest charges to:

- encourage taxpayers to pay their tax liabilities by the due date
- ensure that taxpayers who don't pay their tax liabilities on time don't get an advantage over those who pay in full and on time
- compensate the government for the effect of late payments.

If you receive your notice of amended assessment and incur SIC on the payable amounts, you can request a remission of interest charges. You will need to:

- explain why you think we should remit the interest
- provide evidence to justify your request.

We review each remission application on a case-by-case basis before a decision is made.

sections.heading: Penalties and interest for errors and omissions > Shortfall interest charge deduction
sections.text:
Changes to the law in 2025 means you can no longer claim a deduction for SIC incurred on or after 1 July 2025.

You can claim a deduction for the SIC incurred before 1 July 2025.

You can find the amount of SIC you incurred and paid by checking the statement of account we sent to you.
